title: Install Node.js on Mac
summary: Short article with the steps to install the LTS release of Node.js on macOS and check it worked from the terminal.

concepts.heading: Install steps (macOS)
points: Get the macOS installer from nodejs.org and pick the LTS (Long Term Support) build, the stable option shown on the left of the download page.
Double-click the downloaded .pkg to launch the installer.
On macOS Catalina (10.15) a security warning can block the .pkg. Workaround: Control-click (right-click) the file, choose Open With, then Installer (default).
Accept the licence, keep clicking Next, and leave the default install options.
Verify in the terminal (the course uses Hyper) with node --version; it should print the version number you just installed.

concepts.heading: (Extra) Useful checks
points: (Extra) The installer also adds npm, the package manager used later in this section; npm --version confirms it.
(Extra) If the command is not found, close and reopen the terminal so it picks up the updated PATH.

code_examples.caption: Confirm the install
code_examples.code:
node --version   # e.g. v20.x.x
npm --version    # (Extra) npm ships with Node

pitfalls: Downloading the 'Current' build instead of LTS.
Catalina blocking the .pkg: open it via Control-click > Open With > Installer.
